result.note: Tests the August 2026 IST rules: the 180-day compliance window and NavIC-based domestic time distribution.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Government of India notified rules making Indian Standard Time (IST) the common reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes. Consider the following statements:
items: Organisations have been given 180 days to adapt their systems to the rules.
The government is building domestic time-distribution infrastructure using NavIC and other Indian sources to reduce reliance on foreign satellites.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements match the story. Organisations get a 180-day window to comply, and the government is building time-distribution infrastructure on NavIC, India's satellite navigation system, and other Indian sources. The aim is to cut critical systems' dependence on foreign satellites for timing.
questions.source: The government is also building domestic time-distribution infrastructure using NavIC, India's satellite navigation system, and other Indian sources, reducing critical systems' reliance on foreign satellites.
